title: Methyl-Seq/MRE-Seq
scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic: genomic DNA is split into MspI and HpaII digest branches, library-prepared at the broad level stated by the catalogue, sequenced, aligned and interpreted as a methylation-site result. That paired graph is retained as a family-level depiction; exact applicability to Brunner Methyl-Seq is not protocol-verified from its supplied abstract. A distinct, explicitly text-supported Maunakea MRE-seq variant uses HpaII/AciI/Hin6I parallel digests pooled before library construction and reads out unmethylated restriction-site CpGs. The catalogue shorthand MSRE/MRE-Seq is not treated as a third independently defined implementation. This is an architecture, not a laboratory recipe.

corrections.diagram_observation: The shared Methyl-seq/MRE-Seq overview depicts a two-way split labeled MspI and HpaII, then separate sequence outputs that converge on alignment and an identified methylation site.
corrections.primary_statement: The cited Maunakea MRE-seq implementation instead uses three methylation-sensitive digests (HpaII, AciI and Hin6I), combines their DNA fragments before size selection and library construction, and maps restriction-associated read starts to unmethylated CpGs. The MRE-Seq scope and op_mre_* records are authored from that primary text; the original paired drawing is retained separately.

unknowns.question: Does the Brunner Methyl-Seq primary protocol implement the exact paired MspI/HpaII comparison drawn here, and what digest-derived material is admitted to each library? The supplied abstract and bibliographic metadata cannot resolve this; the relevant primary methods/figure is needed. This limits method-specific assignment, not extraction of the family schematic.

Is the lower-branch intact upper line and interrupted lower line an intentional hemimethylated/nicked substrate representation or a simplified graphic convention? The CCGG cartoons label neither strand polarity nor the modification formula, and the supplied primary text does not resolve this strand-specific picture. An explicit figure legend or primary enzyme/substrate-specific account would be needed for a chemical or strand-resolved claim; the differential-digestion schematic remains interpretable.
